chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Suleym al-Farra', from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who permits the private part of his slave girl for his brother, he said: 'There is no problem with that.' I said, 'Supposing he makes her give birth?' He said: 'His child would be entrusted to him and the slave girl would be returned to her owner.' I said, 'Supposing he had not permitted for him with regards to that?' He said: 'He had permitted that for him, so it was not safe for that to happen.'

key_terms.أَوْلَدَهَا: he made her give birth/impregnated her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man's brother impregnates his slave girl without explicit permission?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *tamlik* (granting sexual access) to a slave girl, establishing that the initial permission implies the right to impregnate, thereby attributing offspring to the brother even without explicit consent for procreation. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the master's act of 'halalizing' the woman transfers the reproductive rights, ensuring the child's lineage is clear and the girl remains the property of the original owner. The hadith underscores the practical legal mechanisms governing concubinage in early Islamic society, distinguishing between ownership rights and paternity attribution.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleym Al Far’a, from Hareyz,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who permitted the private part of his slave girl for his brother. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that’. I said, ‘Supposing he makes her give birth?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His child would be entrusted to him and the slave girl would be returned to her owner’. I said, ‘Supposing he had not permitted for him with regards to that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He had permitted that for him, so it was not safe for that to happen’.
